About

Software engineer by training. Coordinator by practice.

I work at the intersection of technology, business, and execution — helping turn ideas into organised processes, coordinated teams, and meaningful digital outcomes.

I’m a technology professional with a background in Software Engineering and experience spanning technical project coordination, product operations, and digital product delivery.

I’ve collaborated with technical teams, stakeholders, and international clients to organise workflows, coordinate deliverables, support implementation, and keep projects moving.

My engineering background gives me a practical understanding of how digital products are built. My work in product and operations has shaped a second interest: how teams work, how decisions get made, and how ideas become useful solutions.

Beyond delivery, I research responsible AI and natural language processing — specifically gender bias and representation in language technologies for underrepresented languages.

I’m drawn to work that combines thoughtful execution, technology, and meaningful impact.

Research

Who is represented in the data shapes who a language technology serves. My research looks at gender bias and representation in NLP for low-web-data languages, with a focus on Ethiopian and other African languages.

  • Responsible AI
  • Natural language processing
  • Gender bias in language technologies
  • Machine translation
  • Low-resource and low-web-data languages
  • Inclusive AI systems
  • African language technology
Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026

Evaluating Machine Translation Datasets for Low-Web Data Languages: A Gendered Lens

Examines gender representation and bias in machine translation datasets for low-web-data languages, focusing on Ethiopian languages. The work investigates gender imbalances in how datasets are constructed and what they mean for fairness and translation quality.

Read on ACL Anthology
OpenReview

Probing Gender Bias in Masked Language Models for Low-Web Data Languages

Investigates gender bias in masked language models for low-web-data languages, with a focus on underrepresented African languages, contributing to work on fairness, responsible AI, and inclusive NLP.

Read on OpenReview
Leadership & social impact

Youth Advisor, Girl Effect

September 2021 – September 2024

For three years I served on Girl Effect Ethiopia’s youth advisory panel, bringing a young person’s perspective to youth-focused programmes and to conversations about girls’ empowerment and opportunity.

The role was as much about voice as about advice: speaking publicly, advocating, and making sure the people a programme is meant for are part of how it is shaped. The same question — whose voices are represented — runs through my research today.

  • Youth advisory panelGirl Effect Ethiopia, 2021–2024
  • Programme inputIdeas and feedback for programme design, content creation, and impact
  • AdvocacyPublic speaking on girls’ empowerment and opportunities
“I have also been aware of climate change issues and how they are neglected in our community and their impact in our everyday life. I want to be part of the global community fighting and standing up for these issues.”

From a Girl Effect feature on its youth advisory panel members

Speaking for International Day of the Girl.

As part of my advisory work, I spoke for International Day of the Girl — one of the moments where advocacy moves from the meeting room to a public audience.
